verdict_rationale: Все пять дефектов честности закрыты минимально-инвазивно и БЕЗ новой лжи/утечки/PDP-дыры. (а) реестровый дайджест использует БАЙТ-В-БАЙТ тот же READ-PDP путь, что records LIST (getGrantsForSubject + loadTenantOrgAncestry + makeResourceAncestryOracle(orgOracle, emptyRowIndex) + isRecordReadable) — не обходит гейт; мутация «убрать грант-фильтр» делает AC-3 красным (утечка счётчиков чужого реестра поймана). (б) owner-short-circuit проверяет ВЛАДЕЛЬЦА (actorSlug=on-behalf-of user, не агента) через isGenesisOwnerForTenant, читающий role_assignment из БД (NF-3), fail-closed при undefined/throw — не расширяет права агенту; мутация «убрать short-circuit» делает unit AC-4 красным. (в) resolveIdBySlug параметризован ($1/$2), table — compile-time union из литералов (нет инъекции), не найдено → honest op-error не 500; buildHonestOpsReport честно рапортует провалы (мутация «вернуть оптимизм» → AC-7 красный). (г) reply-в-тред + видимый 500 реконсилирован с anti-mask T-0573 §2.2 — существующий anti-mask DB-тест остаётся зелёным, мутация «отключить persist» делает AC-9 красным. (д) телеметрия — не секрет (tenant-scoped process-метрики, уже видны через report-page), keyword-гейт корректно framed как relevance-гейт. Гейты зелёные (build/test/fitness:db/5 single-resolver&anti-case&jargon). Единственный флейк — doc-summary (таймаут под нагрузкой, зелёный изолированно, предупреждён в брифе). Блокирующих находок НЕТ. Замечания — только documentation-hygiene (contract-JSON отстали от BUILD-реконсиляции, но deviations честно задекларированы в pr-handoff) и одна latent within-tenant slug-ambiguity (medium, не security).

findings.title: (а) READ-PDP path is identical to the canonical LIST-records resolver — no bypass
findings.detail: loadReadableRegistryDigest composes getGrantsForSubject + loadTenantOrgAncestry + makeResourceAncestryOracle(orgOracle, emptyRowIndex) and filters each row with isRecordReadable — the SAME four calls as server.ts::resolveReadVisibility (src/server.ts:819-829) used by LIST records. emptyRowIndex means ADR rule-3 (registry/app-scoped narrowing) does not fire — identical to production. Not wider than the actor's READ grants. Mutation proof: disabling the isRecordReadable filter turned AC-3 red at viewerEntry.visibleCount===0 (non-reader would see another registry's count) — the gate is genuinely load-bearing.

findings.title: (б) owner short-circuit checks the USER (not the agent) and is fail-closed
findings.detail: ctx.isTenantOwner wires isGenesisOwnerForTenant(pool, tenantId, actorSlug, now); actorSlug = extractActorSlug(req) = the on-behalf-of USER. isGenesisOwnerForTenant reads role_assignment for role 'tenant-owner' from the DB (NF-3, never from JWT). The subject of the owner check is the user, so it CANNOT widen an agent's rights. try/catch + undefined → owner branch does NOT fire (fail-closed to prior grant check). AC-4 unit test isolates all four branches (owner-true admit, owner-false refuse, undefined refuse, throw refuse). Mutation proof: disabling the short-circuit turned AC-4 red.

findings.title: (в1) resolveIdBySlug: no SQL injection, tenant-scoped
findings.detail: slug + tenantId parameterized ($1/$2); the interpolated `choros.${table}` is a compile-time union "registry_def"|"application" and all 5 call-sites pass string literals — no arbitrary-table surface. UUID passthrough via UUID_RE. Not found → null → honest op-error string (never a 500).

findings.title: (в1) resolveIdBySlug for registry_def is slug-ambiguous across applications within one tenant
findings.detail: registry_def uniqueness is UNIQUE (tenant_id, application_id, slug) — the SAME registry slug can legitimately exist in two different applications in one tenant. resolveIdBySlug does `WHERE tenant_id=$1 AND slug=$2 LIMIT 1` with NO application_id filter and NO ORDER BY, so on a cross-app slug collision it resolves an ARBITRARY (non-deterministic) registry. The configurator could then edit the wrong registry's schema, and buildHonestOpsReport would still show it as ✓ (the op DID succeed — on the wrong target). Application resolution is safe (UNIQUE (tenant_id, slug)). NOT a security hole: strictly within-tenant, within-rights, RLS-enforced — no leak, no escalation. NON-BLOCKING because it requires the specific precondition of a duplicate registry slug across two apps. Follow-up: pass/resolve application_id context, or reject on >1 match rather than LIMIT 1.

findings.title: (а) sample-value leakage into LLM context is bounded to READ-visible business data
findings.detail: pickSampleValue reads only choros.record.data (user-authored business form values), only for PUBLISHED registries, only for rows passing isRecordReadable, truncated to 80 chars, <=3 samples/registry. Secrets (llm_connection credentials, app_secret) and employee PII live in separate tables — never in record.data. Worst case: the actor's own assistant sees field values the actor already may READ (and sees in the UI). Within the столп-6 envelope; not a leak.

findings.title: (г) reply-in-thread does not introduce new duplicate-reply risk on client retry
findings.detail: The user message is persisted with a fresh randomUUID BEFORE dispatch (line 2035). On failure, persistAssistantFailureReply writes one canonical assistant message (fresh UUID) and returns 500. A client retry POSTs a NEW message (new UUID) — same at-least-once append semantics the whole route already has (no idempotency key exists on this route, pre-existing). No NEW dup risk introduced by the failure path.

findings.title: (д) S3-telemetry is tenant-scoped operational data, not a secret — keyword gate is a relevance gate
findings.detail: cycle-time / actor-breakdown are tenant-scoped process metrics already surfaced tenant-wide via report-page-render.ts. No credentials, no cross-tenant data, no PII. isProcessAnalyticsQuery false-negative → telemetry omitted (graceful); false-positive → shows the tenant's own process metrics (mild noise, no confidentiality breach). Correctly framed as relevance, not a security boundary.

findings.title: Contract-JSON artifacts (spec + adr) lag the BUILD-time (г)/(б) reconciliation
findings.detail: spec.contract AC-8 still reads 'runAnalyst ... возвращает HandlerResult с каноническим текстом (без проброса)', but the shipped code and its unit test (assistant-analyst.test.ts:213-215) assert the OPPOSITE — the analyst PROPAGATES (rejects). ADR contract 'Дельта (г)(i)' likewise says runAnalyst 'не пробрасывает' and the route 'отвечает им' (friendly text) — code propagates and responds 500 INTERNAL. ADR 'Дельта (б)' says canOperateSystemAgent runs on 'userGrants на ctx.userSubject, не на пересечении' — code uses ctx.intersectionGrants. ALL THREE drifts are honestly declared in docs/handoff/T-0607.pr-handoff.json deviations_from_adr[0..2], so this is documentation-consistency, NOT deception. Non-blocking. Fix: regenerate the two contract JSONs to match the reconciled implementation.

findings.title: AC-5 (DB) does not isolate the owner short-circuit — the seeded owner also holds authoring_draft
findings.detail: AC-5a's owner comes from registerTenant, which seeds the genesis owner with all 17 mgmt_object grants (incl. authoring_draft). So the owner is admitted via path 2 (canOperateSystemAgent) even with the short-circuit disabled — mutation 2 (disable short-circuit) left AC-5 GREEN while it turned unit AC-4 RED. The short-circuit IS covered (by AC-4 with an empty-intersection owner), so this is a redundant-assertion / test-isolation gap, NOT a coverage hole. Non-blocking. Optional: give AC-5a an owner whose intersection is empty to make the DB test also pin the short-circuit.

No pillar regressed.
